title: χ(3) four-wave mixing
description: Four-wave mixing in a chi(3) waveguide (models/optical_field/waveguide_nl.va with only the Kerr term on): a 50 mW pump at 1310.1145 nm and a 1 mW signal at 1310.1718 nm (two series-stacked CW lasers sharing the 1310 nm WDM reference, 10 GHz apart) co-propagate through 20 mm of n2 = 4.5e-18 m^2/W wire. Nothing about FWM is coded anywhere — the Kerr phase exp(-j*gamma*L*|E(t)|^2) acts on the instantaneous envelope, the pump-signal beat phase-modulates both tones, and two idlers EMERGE on the OSA at exactly 2f_p - f_s (1310.0572 nm, -32 dB below the pump = the textbook phase-matched T*(k*P_p)^2*P_s with k = gamma*L_nl = 3.52 rad/W) and 2f_s - f_p (1310.2290 nm, weaker by exactly P_s/P_p = -17 dB). The time trace shows the 10 GHz envelope beat that drives it all. examples/wg_fwm.py pins the same model to slope-2 pump / slope-1 signal / slope-2 length scaling, XPM/SPM = 2, and the strong-drive Bessel comb, line by line

notes.title: χ(3) four-wave mixing — what this testbench does
lines: Pump laser LP (50 mW, 1310.1145 nm) and signal LS (1 mW,
1310.1718 nm) sit 10 GHz apart, stacked in series, and
co-propagate through 20 mm of chi(3) wire WG1 (Kerr only).
The Kerr phase exp(-j*gamma*L*|E|^2) acts on the envelope;
the pump-signal beat phase-modulates both tones and two
idlers EMERGE at 2f_p-f_s (-32 dB) and 2f_s-f_p (-49 dB).
p_out (spectrum) shows the idlers; p_in is the input,
and the time trace shows the 10 GHz envelope beat.
Set WG1.n2_kerr = 0 and re-run: no Kerr, so no idlers.
